newsitem.title: UK: COPPER - Crunch dates approach as spread nears $30.
newsitem.headline: COPPER - Crunch dates approach as spread nears $30.

text.p: The backwardation for cash to three months copper rose to just under the $300 level during Thursday LME trading, as the tightness swirling fiercely around late-Jan/early-Feb dates intensified.
Cash/threes was indicated at $290/294 at one point today, with this key premium having flared out from around $100 at the start of the year and just over $50 a month ago.

Traders said the tightness, which covers around two weeks, reflects a combination of genuine physical shortages, major short positions from a speculative sell-off in autumn 1996, and merchant players taking advantage of the situation.
"It looks as if could be very nasty, but it will be over very quickly, I think. Some people are going to get hurt, though," one said.
Dates around January 29/30 on the LME were near $20 on Thursday - which compares with the mandatory daily limit which is around $25.
The tightness is taking place against a background of low LME warehouse stocks, which although some way above the recent 6-1/4 year low of 90,050 tonnes, are still scarce, particularly in Europe.
On Tuesday, LME stocks rose 4,725 tonnes to 143,225 tonnes, with the backwardation having attracted some metal in recent weeks.

But the lack of readily available material in Europe has resulted in high premiums being asked for spot physical. Levels of $80 were being sought for LME warrants in Rotterdam, where there is just 5,775 tonnes of copper.
By comparison, there is 38,650 tonnes in Singapore, and Chilean copper warrants there were being offered at nominal levels of just $5.
Traders said that the crucial dates encompass a major U.S. investment house short - built up towards the end of October 1996 when the perception was the market was heading lower.
A European merchant is said to be the major long, and is said by some sources to be taking advantage of the situation.
But an Asian trading house is also believed to have been caught in the net, having fallen astray with a straddle operation in options.
The options were granted to raise revenue, but some of what were the upside calls have moved into-the-money and need delta hedge covereing.
Now short, and showing a loss on some prompts, the house is believed to be asking its LME brokers for extended credit lines, trade sources said.
